source_text: Quot igitur patrocinia naturae, quot privilegia gratiae, quot solemnia disciplinae, figurae, praestructiones, precationes religionem aquae ordinaverunt? Primo quidem, cum populus de Aegypto libere expeditus, vim regis Aegypti, per aquam transgressus, evadit, ipsum regem cum totis copiis aqua exstinxit. Quae figura manifestior in Baptimi sacramento? Liberantur de saeculo nationes per aquam scilicet, et diabolum, dominatorem pristinum, in aqua oppressum derelinquunt. Item aqua de amaritudinis vitio in suum commodum suavitatis Mosei ligno remediatur. Lignum illud erat Christus, venenatae et amarae retro naturae venas insaluberrimas, aquas Baptismi, scilicet, ex sese remedians. Haec est aqua, quae de comite petra populo defluebat. Si enim petra Christus, sine dubio aqua in Christo Baptismum videmus benedici. Quanta aquae gratia penes Deum et Christum ejus est ad Baptismi confirmationem. Nunquam sine aqua Christus, siquidem et ipse aqua tinguitur. Prima rudimenta potestatis suae, vocatus ad nuptias, aqua auspicatur. Cum sermonem facit, sitientes ad aquam suam invitat sempiternam. Cum de agape docet, aquae calicem, fratri oblatum, inter opera dilectionis probat. Apud puteum vires resumit; super aquam incedit libenter, transfretat; aquam discentibus ministrat; perseverat testimonium Baptismi usque ad passionem; cum deditur in crucem, aqua intervenit, sciunt Pilati manus; cum vulneratur, aqua de latere prorumpit, scit lancea militis.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, how many defenses of nature, how many privileges of grace, how many solemnities of discipline, figures, prestructions, and prayers have ordained the religion of water? First, indeed, when the people, having been freely led out of Egypt, crossed through the water, escaped the force of the king of Egypt, and the king himself with all his forces was extinguished by the water. What figure is more manifest in the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, and they leave behind the devil, their former ruler, who is oppressed in the water. Also, the water is remedied from the fault of bitterness by the wood of Moses for its own benefit of sweetness. That wood was Christ, who remedies the most unhealthy veins of a poisonous and bitter nature through the waters of Baptism. This is the water that flowed from the rock, the companion of the people. For if the rock is Christ, then without a doubt, we see the water in Christ blessed for Baptism. How great is the grace of water with God and His Christ for the confirmation of Baptism. Christ is never without water, since He Himself is also baptized with water. The first rudiments of His power are inaugurated with water when He is invited to a wedding. When He preaches, He invites those who thirst to His eternal water. When He teaches about love, He approves the cup of water offered to His brother as one of the works of love. He regains His strength at the well; He walks freely upon the water and crosses it; He serves water to His disciples; He persists in testifying to Baptism until His passion; when He is given over to the cross, water intervenes, as Pilate's hands know; when He is wounded, water bursts forth from His side, as the soldier's lance knows.

pass_b_english: How many defenses of nature, how many privileges of grace, how many solemnities of discipline, figures, prestructions, and prayers have established the religion of water? First, when the people were freely led out of Egypt and crossed through the water, they escaped the force of the king of Egypt, and the king himself with all his forces was extinguished by the water (Exodus 14:28). What figure is more manifest in the sacrament of Baptism? Nations are freed from the world through water, and they leave behind the devil, their former ruler, who is oppressed in the water. Also, water is remedied from the fault of bitterness by the wood of Moses for its own benefit of sweetness (Exodus 15:25). That wood was Christ, who remedies the most unhealthy veins of a poisonous and bitter nature through the waters of Baptism. This is the water that flowed from the companion rock for the people. For if the rock is Christ, then without a doubt we see the water in Christ blessed for Baptism. How great is the grace of water with God and His Christ for the confirmation of Baptism. Christ is never without water, since He Himself is also baptized with water. The first rudiments of His power are inaugurated with water when He is invited to a wedding (John 2:1-11). When He preaches, He invites those who thirst to His eternal water (John 4:14). When He teaches about love, He approves the cup of water offered to a brother as one of the works of love. He regains His strength at the well; He walks freely upon the water and crosses it; He serves water to His disciples; He persists in testifying to Baptism until His passion; when He is given over to the cross, water intervenes, as Pilate's hands know; when He is wounded, water bursts forth from His side, as the soldier's lance knows (John 19:34).
